claim: 1992 Williams introduced REINFORCE as a family of stochastic weight updates for connectionist networks
notes: Not a modern deep RL benchmark paper.

claim: General form Delta w_ij=alpha_ij(r-b_ij)e_ij; e_ij is the score derivative
notes: Baseline conditionally independent of sampled unit output.

claim: When alpha is shared, expected REINFORCE update equals alpha times gradient of expected reinforcement
notes: Requires hypotheses of theorem, not guarantee of monotonic improvement for every sample.

claim: For Bernoulli logistic units the score derivative is (y_i-p_i)x_j
Original episodic REINFORCE uses terminal reinforcement and eligibility summed through time
notes: Distinguish from modern reward-to-go with dense rewards.

claim: Action independent baseline leaves expected policy gradient unchanged
notes: Baseline must not use the sampled action; stop gradients through baseline on actor objective.

claim: Trajectory log probability permits likelihood ratio gradient without differentiating environment transitions
notes: For a finite horizon undiscounted return and theta-independent environment.

claim: Reward-to-go drops rewards from the past in modern VPG derivation
locator: Don't Let the Past Distract You

claim: Policy gradient theorem with function approximation formalizes a larger family after Williams
notes: Do not attribute this theorem to Williams Eq. 11.

claim: Original paper discusses lack of general convergence theory and false optima
Two-action bandit with p=.35, r1=2, r0=0 has exact gradient .455 and zero-variance scalar baseline 1.3
notes: Independent teaching calculation; not an original paper result.

claim: Baseline choice can increase variance even while leaving expected gradient invariant
notes: Zero variance arises only in the deterministic two-action toy.
